title: The integral derived direct image of a constructible complex along a finite-type morphism is constructible
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a $K_0$-morphism (of finite type; separatedness is not assumed) [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an object of the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $Rf_{*,n}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ and
$$
 Rf_*K=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}K_n\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)
$$
be the finite-level and the integral derived direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] being taken of the inverse system with the transition maps specified there. Then $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. More precisely: $Rf_*K$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]; for every $n\geq1$ the finite-reduction comparison $(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\to Rf_{*,n}K_n$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is an isomorphism; $Rf_{*,n}K_n\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]; and if the cohomological supports [def-weil-cohomological-support] of all $K_n$ lie in $[a,b]$, then those of all $Rf_{*,n}K_n$ lie in $[a,b+N]$, where $N$ is an integer (independent of $n$) such that $R^qf_*M=0$ for $q>N$ and every sheaf $M$ of $A_{E,1}$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ (when $K_0$ is algebraically closed, one may take $N=2\dim X$ for nonempty $X$, with Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $N=0$ for empty $X).

Bhatt-Scholze's $D_{cons}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat R)$ (Definition 6.5.1, p. 49) asks the reduction to be constructible with perfect values; the category here asks the reductions to be bounded constructible with finite stalks and a uniform amplitude, so the statement is the analogue of Lemma 6.7.2 for this category, with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\mathfrak m=(\varpi_E)$

proof.text: Set $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$, $P_n=A/I^n$. The coefficient facts [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr, lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] make $A$ a Noetherian domain and every $P_n$ a finite ring. Indeed every ideal in the principal ideal domain $A$ is generated by one element, so it is Noetherian. The resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}A]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is a finite free resolution of $P_n$, since multiplication by the nonzero element $\varpi_E^n$ is injective. Thus every $P_n$ is perfect over $A$, as required in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Its additive group is killed by a power of $\ell$: $\ell$ has positive valuation in $E$, so $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e>0$, and $\ell^r\in I^n$ for $er\geq n$. This order is invertible in $K_0$. The datum therefore applies to exactly the completed coefficient sheaves of the item, rather than to discrete constant $A$-sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9 (3), DVR specialization of the perfect coefficient case

proof.text: Write $\widehat f_*$ for the ordinary unbounded derived pushforward for the completed ring sheaves $\widehat A_X,\widehat A_Y$, as distinct from the integral functor defined by the tower. Their pullback identification is [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. For a $P_n$-complex $C$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the square consisting of $f$ and the identity morphisms of underlying topoi with ring maps $\widehat A_T\to(P_n)_T$. Both composites have the same underlying topos morphism and the same structural ring map, since the finite projections commute with pullback. The identity-topos direct images are restriction of scalars and are exact [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], so their right derived functors are termwise restriction. The two composition isomorphisms give $\widehat f_*\operatorname{Res}_n C\cong\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}C$. Naturality identifies the maps induced by $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ with precisely the tower maps in [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

The hypothesis on $K$ says that its reduction tower has a Roos triangle with first map the family of reductions [def-weil-derived-complete]. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] to this adic datum and $K$. Its commutation with derived limits and the isomorphisms in step 2 identify $\widehat f_*K$ with the tower-defined $Rf_*K$. The same cited statement says that $\widehat f_*K$ is derived complete and that its reduction to $P_n$ is $Rf_{*,n}K_n$, compatibly with quotient transitions. These are the required finite-reduction comparisons: under the limit identification their adjuncts are the $n$-th projections, because the comparison is induced by the reduction unit $K\to\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ and the direct-image/scalar-extension adjunction. Thus it is the comparison specified in [def-weil-derived-direct-image], not merely an unspecified isomorphism between the objects. Transport the Roos triangle through this identification to obtain derived completeness of the tower-defined object.

Fix $n$. The complex $K_n$ is bounded intrinsically constructible by hypothesis. By clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose $L_n\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$ with $\nu_X^*L_n\cong K_n$. This origin lemma allows an arbitrary scheme $T$: its auxiliary global finite-field notation imposes no finite-field structure on $X$ or $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the spectrum of the field $K_0$, $X,Y$ are Noetherian. The inverse image of an affine open under $f$, or under its diagonal, is an open subset of the Noetherian scheme $X$ and hence quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; it need not be separated. Apply [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] with the finite ring $P_n$, killed by a power of the invertible prime $\ell$, to get $Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_n\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$. The bounded-below comparison [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives $Rf_{*,n}K_n\cong\nu_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_n$. The origin equivalence on $Y$ now makes this bounded intrinsically constructible. No finite Tor amplitude over $P_n$ or finite cohomological dimension on all pro-etale sheaves is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, using Theorem 6.7.1 and Lemma 5.4.3; Stacks Tag 09A6 (proetale-lemma-morphism-comparison)

proof.text: There is an integer $N\geq0$ bounding $R^qf_*$ on every torsion etale sheaf by [lem-kun-0f10] (1) and the definition [def-kun-cd]. For any coefficient ring $B$, forgetting $B$-module structure is exact: kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $f$ and the identity-topos ring maps $\mathbf Z\to B$. Both composites have the same structural map, so the underlying abelian complex of $Rf_*^B M$ is the ordinary abelian derived image of the underlying sheaf of $M$. In particular the torsion bound applies to every $P_1$-module sheaf; no bound on the absolute cohomological dimension of $K_0$ is needed. More generally, start with any $N\geq0$ satisfying the $P_1$-module bound in the statement. For a $P_n$-module sheaf $M$, the finite filtration $M\supset\varpi_EM\supset\cdots\supset\varpi_E^nM=0$ has $P_1$-module subquotients. The same composition argument for the quotient map $P_n\to P_1$ identifies their derived images as $P_n$-modules with the exact restrictions of their derived images as $P_1$-modules. Thus the assumed $P_1$ bound applies to these terms in the $P_n$-module derived category. Apply the triangulated derived functor and the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated, lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to each short exact sequence of this filtration. Downward induction on its length gives $R^qf_*M=0$ for all $q>N$. Thus the SAME $N$ works at every finite coefficient level, even though the length of the filtration grows with $n$.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1 and Lemma 6.5.11 (cohomological-dimension input); Stacks Tag 0F10 (etale-cohomology-lemma-finite-cd)

proof.text: If every $K_n$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, the exact pullback in the origin equivalence identifies the cohomology of $L_n$ with that of $K_n$, and clause (i) of the origin equivalence reflects zero constructible sheaves, so $L_n$ also has this range [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin, lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Use the canonical truncation triangle [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] to $\tau_{\leq r}L_n$ for $r=a,a+1,\ldots,b$. Smart truncation leaves cohomology unchanged in the retained degrees and kills the other degrees: at the cut the complex uses the kernel or cokernel of the differential. Hence its upper term has only $\mathcal H^r(L_n)$ in degree $r$; truncating above and below $r$ gives a quasi-isomorphism with the one-term complex. Its upper term is $\mathcal H^r(L_n)[-r]$ (represented by the one-term complex), and the lower term has range $[a,r-1]$. The derived image of a sheaf in degree $r$ has range $[r,r+N]$, by left exactness and step 5. Apply the triangulated functor and [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Starting with zero below $a$, induction shows that the image of the truncation through degree $r$ has range $[a,r+N]$: outside this interval both outside terms of the long exact sequence vanish. At $r=b$ this proves $Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_n$ has range $[a,b+N]$. Pullback is exact and the comparison in step 4 identifies it with $Rf_{*,n}K_n$, giving the desired uniform interval. This is a finite truncation argument; it uses no unbounded spectral-sequence convergence assertion.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, finite-level boundedness argument (finite truncation devissage)

proof.text: Suppose $K_0$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is nonempty, of dimension $d$. It is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives base-field torsion cohomological dimension zero. For a geometric point of $Y$, the pointed etale neighbourhoods may be chosen affine and of finite presentation over $Y$. Then $X_W=X\times_YW$ is finite-type over $K_0$ and etale over $X$. If $X_W$ is empty its cohomology groups are zero, since its abelian sheaf category is zero. Otherwise apply the following dimension argument to this nonempty $X_W$. The local dimension equality [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_W,x'}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq d$. A chain of specializations is counted in the local ring at its last point, so the supremum of these local dimensions bounds the dimension of $X_W$ by $d$. By [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd], $H^q((X_W)_{\mathrm{et}},M)=0$ for every torsion sheaf and $q>2d$. Each group in the stalk test [lem-kun-cd-stalk-criterion] is therefore zero in those degrees. The test proves $R^qf_*M=0$ for $q>2d$, so one may choose $N=2d$. For $X=\varnothing$ all direct images are zero and one takes $N=0$; this is the separate empty-case bound in the corrected statement, since the Krull dimension of the empty space is $-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1, dimension bound via etale neighbourhoods; Stacks Tag 07QP (more-algebra-lemma-dimension-etale-extension)

proof.text: Finally, the definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] requires precisely derived completeness, constructibility of every finite reduction, and one finite cohomological interval containing all reductions. Step 3 supplies completeness and identifies these reductions with the complexes of step 4; step 6 supplies the interval $[a,b+N]$, with $[a,b]$ provided by the hypothesis $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Hence the tower-defined $Rf_*K$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and all the more precise clauses hold.
